The biggest issue is the media: about 690 MB of videos, some of them over 80 MB each, which will make the site slow, especially on phones.

20: ## What the project is
21: 
22: - **No build step.** It's just `index.html`, `styles.css`, `script.js` and `gallery-data.js`. GitHub Pages serves them as they are, and `.nojekyll` tells it not to process them.
23: - **`index.html` (~760 lines)** holds all the page sections: header, hero, a skills ticker, About, Projects, Skills, Experience, Resume, Contact, and two pop-up windows (project details and profile photo).
24: - **`gallery-data.js`** is where the project content lives. It defines six project entries, each with a cover image, tags, notes, optional links and a list of media:
25:   - DiJoker (company games)
26:   - TroubleFixIt
27:   - Disaster Game
28:   - Build2Connect
29:   - 3D Basketball
30:   - Prototype Lab
31: - **`script.js`** builds the page from that data. It handles:
32:   - the auto-rotating video reel at the top, with its "Showcase Reel" / "R&D Track" switch
33:   - the project cards, and the pop-up gallery with Prev/Next, thumbnails and keyboard support
34:   - fade-in effects as you scroll, and the header hiding after you scroll
35:   - respecting the "reduce motion" setting
36: - **`styles.css` (~2,050 lines)** uses a dark theme with Google Fonts. Its mobile layouts kick in at 1100px, 860px and 620px wide.
37: - **Assets:** 59 files, including a resume PDF, a resume preview image, screenshots and game footage.
38: 
39: ## Findings to address later
40: 
41: **Performance (highest impact)**
42: - Six videos are 60–82 MB each, including the Build2Connect cutscene and two of the basketball clips.
43: - The top reel loads every clip twice, once for the visible video and once for the blurred background, and switches clips every 3 seconds. On mobile, that can download hundreds of MB.
44: - The fix is to re-encode the clips as short, compressed 720p versions (around 2–8 MB each) and add poster images.
45: 
46: **Repository size**
47: - The git history is already 545 MB. GitHub warns about files over 50 MB, rejects files over 100 MB, and recommends keeping repos under about 1 GB. Every new raw recording pushes it closer.
48: - Git LFS isn't set up, and plain re-encoding won't shrink the history that's already there.
49: 
50: **Unused files (about 136 MB that nothing on the site points to)**
51: - `assets/showcase/dijoker-demo.mp4`, `pc-building-demo.mp4` and `pixel-pass-demo.mp4` are copies of other clips.
52: - `assets/showcase/pc-building-shot.png` and `assets/CV - Francis Yambao_page-0001.jpg` aren't used either.
53: 
54: **Code tidy-ups**
55: - `updateHeroMontage` in `script.js` is never called, and its caption says "randomized every 2s" when the reel actually advances every 3 seconds in order.
56: - The "R&D Track" reel only filters out DiJoker, so it also shows TroubleFixIt, Disaster Game and Build2Connect. Those are commissioned or finished projects, not R&D.
57: - The header hides as soon as you scroll and there's no navigation menu, so visitors can only move around through the in-page buttons.
58: 
59: **Discoverability and accessibility**
60: - There are no Open Graph or Twitter preview tags, so links shared on LinkedIn or Messenger won't show a preview image.
61: - The pop-up windows don't keep keyboard focus inside them while open.
62: - Most media labels are generic, like "Editor screenshot 01" or "R&D capture 02".
63: 
64: **Content and naming**
65: - File names are long raw names from Facebook or screen recorders, such as `469523681_1222...n.jpg` and `Boobies Trap - Opera 2026-...mp4`. Since that recording's file name is public, you may want to rename it.
66: - Your phone number is published in two places on the page; that's fine if it's intentional.

1802: ## Findings
1803: 
1804: Code-built primitives can't get much closer to the guide. Anime characters like this are modeled by hand or generated by AI, then shaded with special toon tricks. There are four realistic paths; they can be combined.
1805: 
1806: **1. VRoid Studio (free, anime-specific): best match for the face and hair**
1807: - It's a desktop app built only for anime characters. You get real anime eyes, layered hair, blink and smile expressions, and a humanoid skeleton.
1808: - It exports a `.vrm` file, a glTF-based character format. Three.js loads it with [`@pixiv/three-vrm`](https://pixiv.github.io/three-vrm/docs/), which brings the MToon anime shader with outlines, rim light and painted shading.
1809: - You would build Niko with its sliders (big head, short body for chibi proportions, brown spiky hair, cloak). I would then wire it into the world, including walk, idle and the intro flip.
1810: - Downside: it looks smooth anime rather than faceted low-poly.
1811: 
1812: **2. AI image-to-3D ([Meshy anime generator](https://www.meshy.ai/3d-tools/anime-character-generator), [Tripo](https://www.tripo3d.ai/features/image-to-3d-model/for-3d-character), [Hunyuan3D](https://hunyuan3d.cc/)): closest to the guide's 3D style**
1813: - You upload the front turnaround from the guide and get a textured, auto-rigged GLB in about a minute. Meshy and Tripo both have a low-poly or "smart mesh" option.
1814: - These need an account and credits, so you'd generate the model. Expect some cleanup, usually skin weights and face texture.
1815: 
1816: **3. Blender plus [Blender MCP](https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp): lets me drive Blender from Cursor**
1817: - Install Blender, `uv` and the add-on, then add the MCP server in Cursor Settings → MCP. On Windows the command is `cmd /c uvx blender-mcp`.
1818: - I could then clean up a generated model: reduce the polygon count, transfer face normals for anime shading, bake textures, and export GLB.
1819: - Its limit: AI can't sculpt or paint well, so it's for cleanup and export, not making the character from scratch.
1820: 
1821: **4. Rendering tricks I can add now, with no tools**
1822: - **Inverted-hull ink outline:** a copy of each mesh drawn slightly larger in dark ink. This is the biggest single anime cue.
1823: - **Anime face normals:** make the face's lighting normals all point forward, so the face shades as one flat painted plane. That fixes "round head, flat face" ([custom normals workflow](http://www.aversionofreality.com/blog/2022/4/21/custom-normals-workflow)).
1824: - Smooth-shaded hair with a cel highlight band, and a 3-band skin ramp.
1825: 
1826: **About `file://`:** any model file (GLB or VRM) would break opening the page from disk. I can embed the model inside `world.bundle.js` at build time so it keeps working.

If you deploy the repo root, `.personalinfo/`, `.cursor/` or `.impeccable/` could be reachable by URL. Add a `.vercelignore` that lists them, or deploy only the site files. GitHub Pages hides those folders today only because it runs Jekyll, which skips dot folders.

The free tiers cap monthly bandwidth, and your raw videos are 20–80 MB each, so re-encoding them to web size becomes more important. Vercel Hobby is also for non-commercial use only, which a portfolio fits.

1: # 3D models: how to regenerate, recreate, or import them
2: 
3: Guide for AI agents working on this repo. Read it before you replace Niko, add a prop from a reference link, or redo a model.
4: Project rules still apply (`.cursor/rules/core-memory.mdc`): edit `world.js`, then always run `node .impeccable/tools/build-world.mjs`; CRLF in js/html; never commit unless asked.
5: 
6: ## 1. Pick the route first
7: 
8: | What you were given | Route |
9: | --- | --- |
10: | A link to someone else's model (Sketchfab, ArtStation, a store page) | **B**: recreate it as an original procedural model (route **A**). Download it only if its licence allows it (see section 3). |
11: | A Tripo Studio link to a model the user generated | **C**: fetch the user's GLB, decode it, clean it, wire it in. |
12: | A GLB the user dropped into `assets/` | **C**, starting from "Cleanup" (section 4.4). |
13: | "Make a sword / prop / rock like X" with no file | **A**: write a generator script. |
14: 
15: Never guess. If the user's wording could mean "copy that file" or "make one like it", recreate it (route A) and say so.
16: 
17: ## 2. Route A: procedural GLB generator (how the xiphos sword was made)
18: 
19: Reference implementations: `.impeccable/tools/xiphos-sword.mjs` writes `assets/models/xiphos-sword.glb`,
20: and `.impeccable/tools/longsword.mjs` writes `assets/models/longsword.glb` (run either from the repo root).
21: 
22: The Sketchfab Longsword by shor.riot (2,524 triangles / 1,531 vertices) is not downloadable, its public API does
23: not list a licence, and its page is marked NoAI. The project prop is a generic original weathered-steel longsword
24: with a fuller, iron crossguard, wrapped grip, and faceted pommel; it does not include the source mesh, textures, or
25: distinctive ornament.
26: 
27: ### 2.1 Collect the brief from the reference page
28: 
29: From the reference page, write down the facts that define the look: triangle count, vertex count, texture size,
30: materials, and the author's own description. Example, for the Sketchfab xiphos the user linked:
31: - 718 triangles / 424 vertices, 256×256 hand-painted diffuse textures, PS2/GameCube "stylized realism".
32: - Leaf-shaped bronze blade with patina, heavily worn iron hilt.
33: 
34: Turn that into a shape spec: silhouette (profile stations), cross-section, parts, and palette. Do not trace or download
35: their mesh.
36: 
37: ### 2.2 Build it in a script, not by hand
38: 
39: The pattern in `xiphos-sword.mjs`:
40: - `@gltf-transform/core` `Document` + `NodeIO` writes the GLB; geometry comes from the vendored three
41:   (`../../vendor/three/three.module.min.js`): `LatheGeometry` for round parts (grip, pommel), `ExtrudeGeometry` for flat
42:   outlines (guard), and hand-built ring lofts for blades (a profile table `[t, halfWidth, halfThickness]` × a cross-section ring).
43: - Low-poly look = **faceted**: `geometry.toNonIndexed()` then `computeVertexNormals()`, so every triangle is flat.
44: - "Hand-painted" textures = SVG drawn in code and rasterised by `sharp` (gradients, blurred blotches for patina/rust,
45:   pits, scratches). Use a **seeded** random so every build is identical. Keep textures small (64–256 px).
46: - UVs: blades get u across the width and v along the length (v = 0 at the base; glTF image row 0 is v = 0).
47:   Tiling parts use a side projection (`boxUv`) so the texel density matches across pieces.
48: - Units and pivot: +Y up along the object's main axis, origin where it is held or stands. The xiphos origin is near
49:   the pommel, the guard face at y ≈ 0.2, the tip at y ≈ 0.92, and the grip centre at y = 0.1 (`SWORD_GRIP_Y` in `world.js`).
50: - Log the triangle count at the end and keep it near the reference (xiphos: 556 vs the reference's 718).
51: 
52: ### 2.3 Preview before wiring
53: 
54: Server: `node .impeccable/tools/serve.mjs 8765` (repo root, background). Then, from `.impeccable/tools`:
55: 
56: ```
57: node model-view.mjs /assets/models/<file>.glb <prefix>   # writes ../review/<prefix>-{front,side,iso,top}.png
58: ```
59: 
60: Read the PNGs. The image tool caches by path, so use a new prefix every time.
61: 
62: ### 2.4 Wire it into the world
63: 
64: See the sword pickup blocks in `world.js`:
65: - `import xiphosGlb from "./assets/models/<file>.glb";`. esbuild's binary loader embeds it in `world.bundle.js`, so `file://` still works.
66: - Parse with `new GLTFLoader().parseAsync(buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset + buf.byteLength), "")`.
67: - Swap materials to the island look: `node.material = softMapped(node.material.map)`, with `castShadow` and `receiveShadow` on.
68: - Size it against Niko: he is about 2.2 world units tall (2.5 units ≈ 1.5 m). The xiphos is `SWORD_SIZE` 1.15 world units.
69: - Place it with `island.spot(...)`, `landing`, or offsets in **screen terms**: the default camera's screen-right is
70:   `(+1, 0, −1)/√2` and up-screen (away from the camera) is `(−1, 0, −1)/√2`. Snap the spot to walkable ground with
71:   `island.nav.walkable` / `island.nav.nearest`, and set its height with `island.groundAt`.
72: - Things Niko holds are parented to a bone. `fitSwordGrip()` builds the grip from the knuckle bones
73:   (`RightHandIndex1/Pinky1/Middle1/Thumb1`). They are children of `RightHand`, so the fit holds in every clip.
74:   The blade runs along the knuckle line, dipped toward the fingers, with its flat facing the palm.
75: - Both the Xiphos and longsword have independent ground placements and pickup state. The longsword uses Niko's left
76:   hand so the two swords can be collected separately and held together.
77: - Add a `debug` hook (`debug.sword()` / `debug.longsword()`, pass `true` to equip either) and a Puppeteer check
78:   (`sword-check.mjs` / `longsword-check.mjs`).
79: - Remember: from the 45° top-down camera, a blade pointing straight at the viewer looks like it hangs down. Confirm
80:   directions numerically (bone world axes) before "fixing" what a screenshot seems to show.
81: 
82: ## 3. Route B: a model from someone else's page
83: 
84: 1. Open the page and read its licence and "Download" state.
85:    - Downloads disabled, or no licence: **do not** fetch it from network requests or a HAR capture. Recreate it with route A.
86:      The repo has done this before: the training dummy (iltaen's Sketchfab dummy had downloads off) and the xiphos.
87:    - Downloadable and CC0 / CC-BY (Sketchfab "Download 3D model"): download the glTF/GLB, keep the credit,
88:      and still restyle it to the island look. `assets/niko/hair-short.glb` is a Sketchfab cap that came in as a download.
89: 2. Reference downloads go in `assets/sampleModels/` (reference only, never shipped; `.vercelignore` excludes it).
90: 3. Tell the user which one you did.
91: 
92: ## 4. Route C: Tripo (how Niko's body was made)
93: 
94: ### 4.1 History, so you do not redo dead ends
95: 
96: - The user generates characters in **Tripo Studio** (`studio.tripo3d.ai`) from the character art in `assets/`
97:   (`Niko_ Child of the Star Character Guide.png`, `Low-Poly Starry Mage Explorer.png` and its `.glb` in `assets/sampleModels/`).
98:   Page slugs like `low-poly-humanoid-character-with-light-skin-and-dark-gray-shorts-8a00cde2-…` are Tripo's own captions.
99: - First Tripo body (task `8a00cde2…`): low-poly humanoid, **6,264 triangles / 7,262 vertices**, one base-colour texture,
100:   Mixamo skeleton with the `mixamorig:` prefix, **no animation clips**, faces **+X**, arms along Z, origin at the feet,
101:   about 0.98 units tall. Saved plain as `assets/niko/low-poly-humanoid.glb`.
102: - `assets/niko/fantasy-character-7k.glb`: a second Tripo character (task `868144a6…`). Its PBR source was 1.9 M triangles;
103:   it was simplified to 7,000 faces with meshoptimizer (section 4.3). It is not in the game.
104: - `low-poly-humanoid-v2…v6.glb` are the user's own iterations (v2 came from a Tripo `3d-model/...47ce7efe…` page; v6 is a
105:   Blender face edit). **`low-poly-humanoid-v6-clean.glb` is the body in the game** (v6 run through section 4.4).
106: - Rejected, do not repeat: sculpting the face in code (nose/jaw/brow vertex pushes), the older procedural mascot as the
107:   main body, and baking clips into the GLB (clips are retargeted at load instead).
108: 
109: ### 4.2 Getting the GLB out of Tripo
110: 
111: Preferred: ask the user to export it from Tripo with these settings:
112: - Format **GLB** (not FBX/OBJ/USDZ). Mesh: **low-poly / smart mesh**, about 5k–20k triangles.
113: - **Auto-rig: humanoid/biped (Mixamo-compatible)**. T-pose or A-pose, facing forward.
114: - Textures embedded, 1024–2048 px (4K is wasted at this camera distance).
115: - Then save it in `assets/niko/` with a new version suffix. Never overwrite the user's file.
116: 
117: If the user asks you to fetch it from a Tripo page they own:
118: 1. Open the workspace page in the browser tool and let the viewer load.
119: 2. The viewer streams a **signed, meshopt-compressed GLB** from CloudFront:
120:    `https://tripo-data.rg1.data.tripo3d.com/tripo-studio/<yyyymmdd>/<taskId>/tripo_<pbr_model|rigging>_<taskId>_meshopt.glb?Key-Pair-Id=…&Policy=…&Signature=…`
121:    Find it with `performance.getEntriesByType("resource").map((e) => e.name).filter((u) => /tripo-data.*\.glb/.test(u))`,
122:    or by searching the page HTML. The `rigging` file is the rigged low-poly; `pbr_model` is the high-poly textured mesh.
123:    A `output_point_cloud_…glb` is not the mesh.
124: 3. Download it with **node `fetch`** and write the bytes to a file. Do not use PowerShell `curl` (it is Invoke-WebRequest),
125:    and do not pass the URL through a shell (the `~` in signatures gets mangled). Signed URLs expire, so download right away.
126:    Do not commit or paste the signed URL into docs.
127: 4. If a quad/retopo mesh is shown in the viewer but never appears in the resources, do not block on it. Simplify locally (4.3).
128: 
129: ### 4.3 Decode, and simplify if needed
130: 
131: Run scripts from `.impeccable/tools` (that is where `@gltf-transform/*`, `meshoptimizer`, `sharp` and `puppeteer-core` are installed).
132: 
133: ```js
134: import { NodeIO } from "@gltf-transform/core";
135: import { ALL_EXTENSIONS } from "@gltf-transform/extensions";
136: import { MeshoptDecoder } from "meshoptimizer";
137: await MeshoptDecoder.ready;
138: const doc = await new NodeIO().registerExtensions(ALL_EXTENSIONS).registerDependencies({ "meshopt.decoder": MeshoptDecoder }).read(src);
139: await new NodeIO().write(out, doc); // a FRESH NodeIO: one that registered meshopt but has no encoder throws encodeGltfBuffer
140: ```
141: 
142: "Some extensions were not registered for I/O" on write is expected, and the texture still writes.
143: 
144: Simplifying (how the 7k fantasy character was made): `MeshoptSimplifier.simplifyWithAttributes(indices, positions, 3,
145: uvs, 2, [highUvWeight, highUvWeight], null, targetFaces * 3, 1, [])`. Strides are in floats, the target index count must be a
146: multiple of 3, `target_error` up to 1 so the count is actually reached, and the UV weight is high so the texture does not swim.
147: Then `compactMesh`, and write a plain GLB with the original JPEG material.
148: 
149: ### 4.4 Cleanup (every new body goes through this)
150: 
151: From `.impeccable/tools`:
152: 
153: ```
154: python tex-pad.py ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
155: node mesh-clean.mjs ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb --texture ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
156: python mesh-audit.py ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb [yMin]
157: ```
158: 
159: - `tex-pad.py` fills the black gaps between UV islands with the nearest island colour, so seams and mipmaps don't go dark.
160: - `mesh-clean.mjs` drops degenerate triangles, fills small holes, and collapses only tiny folded slivers. Larger folds,
161:   like the shorts hem, are intentional; collapsing them made non-manifold edges. It also recomputes smooth normals shared
162:   across UV seams, and **removes Blender's duplicate unused armature**. A second skin with the same bone names steals the
163:   animation binding, and the body then stays in bind pose. UVs, skin weights and texture are left alone.
164: - Aim for 0 open edges, 0 non-manifold edges and 0 seam normal breaks in the audit.
165: 
166: ### 4.5 Putting a body in the game
167: 
168: All in `useNikoModel` (`world.js`):
169: - Swap `import nikoBody from "./assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb";`. The body is scaled to `PREVIOUS_HEIGHT` 2.17 and yawed
170:   `-Math.PI / 2` (Tripo faces +X; the game walks +Z), with the origin planted at the soles.
171: - Animation is **not** in the GLB. `retargetMixamo` plays `assets/niko/Idle.fbx` and `assets/Running (1).fbx` on any body
172:   with Mixamo bone names. `mixamorig` is stripped on the **target only**; hips keep only their vertical bob.
173: - Lock-on strafes come from `assets/niko/lockon.json` (Pixel Pass Unity `.anim` curves via `lockon-clips.mjs`). Unity
174:   arm curves need the y/z sign flip in `curvesClip` or the wrists cross.
175: - Eyes are painted decals from `assets/niko-eyes.png`, fitted with `EYE_FIT` (`debug.eyes`, `face-fit.mjs`). Hair is
176:   `hair-short.glb` seated on the Head bone (`HAIR_FIT`, `debug.hair`).
177: - An embedded textured body grows the bundle by roughly its file size. Keep bodies around 1.5 MB.
178: 
179: ### 4.6 Verify
180: 
181: - `niko-walk.mjs`, `niko-angles.mjs`, `face-fit.mjs`, `niko-light.mjs` (all in `.impeccable/tools`, screenshots in `.impeccable/review/`).
182: - Prove animation numerically: a bone quaternion changes while a key is held, and the skinned mesh's skeleton bone is the
183:   same object as `bot.bones.<name>`. Screenshot descriptions have invented T-poses before.
184: - `python mesh-audit.py` on the shipped file.
185: 
186: ## 5. Tool index (`.impeccable/tools`)
187: 
188: | Tool | Use |
189: | --- | --- |
190: | `xiphos-sword.mjs` | Procedural GLB template (run from the repo root) |
191: | `longsword.mjs` | Procedural longsword GLB generator (run from the repo root) |
192: | `model-view.mjs <url> <prefix>` | Front, side, iso and top shots of any GLB served on :8765 |
193: | `glb-shots.mjs`, `pose-shot.mjs` | Character GLB shots (clips, hands, face) |
194: | `glb-dump.mjs` | Dump a GLB's nodes, materials and textures |
195: | `tex-pad.py`, `mesh-clean.mjs`, `mesh-audit.py` | Body cleanup and audit |
196: | `sword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | In-game pickup and grip shots |
197: | `longsword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | Longsword pickup and left-hand grip check |

1: # 3D models: how to regenerate, recreate, or import them
2: 
3: Guide for AI agents working on this repo. Read it before you replace Niko, add a prop from a reference link, or redo a model.
4: Project rules still apply (`.cursor/rules/core-memory.mdc`): edit `world.js`, then always run `node .impeccable/tools/build-world.mjs`; CRLF in js/html; never commit unless asked.
5: 
6: ## 1. Pick the route first
7: 
8: | What you were given | Route |
9: | --- | --- |
10: | A link to someone else's model (Sketchfab, ArtStation, a store page) | **B**: recreate it as an original procedural model (route **A**). Download it only if its licence allows it (see section 3). |
11: | A Tripo Studio link to a model the user generated | **C**: fetch the user's GLB, decode it, clean it, wire it in. |
12: | A GLB the user dropped into `assets/` | **C**, starting from "Cleanup" (section 4.4). |
13: | "Make a sword / prop / rock like X" with no file | **A**: write a generator script. |
14: 
15: Never guess. If the user's wording could mean "copy that file" or "make one like it", recreate it (route A) and say so.
16: 
17: ## 2. Route A: procedural GLB generator (how the xiphos sword was made)
18: 
19: Reference implementations: `.impeccable/tools/xiphos-sword.mjs` writes `assets/models/xiphos-sword.glb`,
20: and `.impeccable/tools/longsword.mjs` writes `assets/models/longsword.glb` (run either from the repo root).
21: 
22: The Sketchfab Longsword by shor.riot (2,524 triangles / 1,531 vertices) is not downloadable, its public API does
23: not list a licence, and its page is marked NoAI. The project prop is a generic original weathered-steel longsword
24: with a fuller, iron crossguard, wrapped grip, and faceted pommel; it does not include the source mesh, textures, or
25: distinctive ornament.
26: 
27: ### 2.1 Collect the brief from the reference page
28: 
29: From the reference page, write down the facts that define the look: triangle count, vertex count, texture size,
30: materials, and the author's own description. Example, for the Sketchfab xiphos the user linked:
31: - 718 triangles / 424 vertices, 256×256 hand-painted diffuse textures, PS2/GameCube "stylized realism".
32: - Leaf-shaped bronze blade with patina, heavily worn iron hilt.
33: 
34: Turn that into a shape spec: silhouette (profile stations), cross-section, parts, and palette. Do not trace or download
35: their mesh.
36: 
37: ### 2.2 Build it in a script, not by hand
38: 
39: The pattern in `xiphos-sword.mjs`:
40: - `@gltf-transform/core` `Document` + `NodeIO` writes the GLB; geometry comes from the vendored three
41:   (`../../vendor/three/three.module.min.js`): `LatheGeometry` for round parts (grip, pommel), `ExtrudeGeometry` for flat
42:   outlines (guard), and hand-built ring lofts for blades (a profile table `[t, halfWidth, halfThickness]` × a cross-section ring).
43: - Low-poly look = **faceted**: `geometry.toNonIndexed()` then `computeVertexNormals()`, so every triangle is flat.
44: - "Hand-painted" textures = SVG drawn in code and rasterised by `sharp` (gradients, blurred blotches for patina/rust,
45:   pits, scratches). Use a **seeded** random so every build is identical. Keep textures small (64–256 px).
46: - UVs: blades get u across the width and v along the length (v = 0 at the base; glTF image row 0 is v = 0).
47:   Tiling parts use a side projection (`boxUv`) so the texel density matches across pieces.
48: - Units and pivot: +Y up along the object's main axis, origin where it is held or stands. The xiphos origin is near
49:   the pommel, the guard face at y ≈ 0.2, the tip at y ≈ 0.92, and the grip centre at y = 0.1 (`SWORD_GRIP_Y` in `world.js`).
50: - Log the triangle count at the end and keep it near the reference (xiphos: 556 vs the reference's 718).
51: 
52: ### 2.3 Preview before wiring
53: 
54: Server: `node .impeccable/tools/serve.mjs 8765` (repo root, background). Then, from `.impeccable/tools`:
55: 
56: ```
57: node model-view.mjs /assets/models/<file>.glb <prefix>   # writes ../review/<prefix>-{front,side,iso,top}.png
58: ```
59: 
60: Read the PNGs. The image tool caches by path, so use a new prefix every time.
61: 
62: ### 2.4 Wire it into the world
63: 
64: See the sword pickup blocks in `world.js`:
65: - `import xiphosGlb from "./assets/models/<file>.glb";`. esbuild's binary loader embeds it in `world.bundle.js`, so `file://` still works.
66: - Parse with `new GLTFLoader().parseAsync(buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset + buf.byteLength), "")`.
67: - Swap materials to the island look: `node.material = softMapped(node.material.map)`, with `castShadow` and `receiveShadow` on.
68: - Size it against Niko: he is about 2.2 world units tall (2.5 units ≈ 1.5 m). The xiphos is `SWORD_SIZE` 1.15 world units.
69: - Place it with `island.spot(...)`, `landing`, or offsets in **screen terms**: the default camera's screen-right is
70:   `(+1, 0, −1)/√2` and up-screen (away from the camera) is `(−1, 0, −1)/√2`. Snap the spot to walkable ground with
71:   `island.nav.walkable` / `island.nav.nearest`, and set its height with `island.groundAt`.
72: - Things Niko holds are parented to a bone. `fitSwordGrip()` builds the grip from the knuckle bones
73:   (`RightHandIndex1/Pinky1/Middle1/Thumb1`). They are children of `RightHand`, so the fit holds in every clip.
74:   The blade runs along the knuckle line, dipped toward the fingers, with its flat facing the palm.
75: - Both the Xiphos and longsword have independent ground placements and pickup state. The longsword uses Niko's left
76:   hand so the two swords can be collected separately and held together.
77: - Add a `debug` hook (`debug.sword()` / `debug.longsword()`, pass `true` to equip either) and a Puppeteer check
78:   (`sword-check.mjs` / `longsword-check.mjs`).
79: - Remember: from the 45° top-down camera, a blade pointing straight at the viewer looks like it hangs down. Confirm
80:   directions numerically (bone world axes) before "fixing" what a screenshot seems to show.
81: 
82: ## 3. Route B: a model from someone else's page
83: 
84: 1. Open the page and read its licence and "Download" state.
85:    - Downloads disabled, or no licence: **do not** fetch it from network requests or a HAR capture. Recreate it with route A.
86:      The repo has done this before: the training dummy (iltaen's Sketchfab dummy had downloads off) and the xiphos.
87:    - Downloadable and CC0 / CC-BY (Sketchfab "Download 3D model"): download the glTF/GLB, keep the credit,
88:      and still restyle it to the island look. `assets/niko/hair-short.glb` is a Sketchfab cap that came in as a download.
89: 2. Reference downloads go in `assets/sampleModels/` (reference only, never shipped; `.vercelignore` excludes it).
90: 3. Tell the user which one you did.
91: 
92: ## 4. Route C: Tripo (how Niko's body was made)
93: 
94: ### 4.1 History, so you do not redo dead ends
95: 
96: - The user generates characters in **Tripo Studio** (`studio.tripo3d.ai`) from the character art in `assets/`
97:   (`Niko_ Child of the Star Character Guide.png`, `Low-Poly Starry Mage Explorer.png` and its `.glb` in `assets/sampleModels/`).
98:   Page slugs like `low-poly-humanoid-character-with-light-skin-and-dark-gray-shorts-8a00cde2-…` are Tripo's own captions.
99: - First Tripo body (task `8a00cde2…`): low-poly humanoid, **6,264 triangles / 7,262 vertices**, one base-colour texture,
100:   Mixamo skeleton with the `mixamorig:` prefix, **no animation clips**, faces **+X**, arms along Z, origin at the feet,
101:   about 0.98 units tall. Saved plain as `assets/niko/low-poly-humanoid.glb`.
102: - `assets/niko/fantasy-character-7k.glb`: a second Tripo character (task `868144a6…`). Its PBR source was 1.9 M triangles;
103:   it was simplified to 7,000 faces with meshoptimizer (section 4.3). It is not in the game.
104: - `low-poly-humanoid-v2…v6.glb` are the user's own iterations (v2 came from a Tripo `3d-model/...47ce7efe…` page; v6 is a
105:   Blender face edit). **`low-poly-humanoid-v6-clean.glb` is the body in the game** (v6 run through section 4.4).
106: - Rejected, do not repeat: sculpting the face in code (nose/jaw/brow vertex pushes), the older procedural mascot as the
107:   main body, and baking clips into the GLB (clips are retargeted at load instead).
108: 
109: ### 4.2 Getting the GLB out of Tripo
110: 
111: Preferred: ask the user to export it from Tripo with these settings:
112: - Format **GLB** (not FBX/OBJ/USDZ). Mesh: **low-poly / smart mesh**, about 5k–20k triangles.
113: - **Auto-rig: humanoid/biped (Mixamo-compatible)**. T-pose or A-pose, facing forward.
114: - Textures embedded, 1024–2048 px (4K is wasted at this camera distance).
115: - Then save it in `assets/niko/` with a new version suffix. Never overwrite the user's file.
116: 
117: If the user asks you to fetch it from a Tripo page they own:
118: 1. Open the workspace page in the browser tool and let the viewer load.
119: 2. The viewer streams a **signed, meshopt-compressed GLB** from CloudFront:
120:    `https://tripo-data.rg1.data.tripo3d.com/tripo-studio/<yyyymmdd>/<taskId>/tripo_<pbr_model|rigging>_<taskId>_meshopt.glb?Key-Pair-Id=…&Policy=…&Signature=…`
121:    Find it with `performance.getEntriesByType("resource").map((e) => e.name).filter((u) => /tripo-data.*\.glb/.test(u))`,
122:    or by searching the page HTML. The `rigging` file is the rigged low-poly; `pbr_model` is the high-poly textured mesh.
123:    A `output_point_cloud_…glb` is not the mesh.
124: 3. Download it with **node `fetch`** and write the bytes to a file. Do not use PowerShell `curl` (it is Invoke-WebRequest),
125:    and do not pass the URL through a shell (the `~` in signatures gets mangled). Signed URLs expire, so download right away.
126:    Do not commit or paste the signed URL into docs.
127: 4. If a quad/retopo mesh is shown in the viewer but never appears in the resources, do not block on it. Simplify locally (4.3).
128: 
129: ### 4.3 Decode, and simplify if needed
130: 
131: Run scripts from `.impeccable/tools` (that is where `@gltf-transform/*`, `meshoptimizer`, `sharp` and `puppeteer-core` are installed).
132: 
133: ```js
134: import { NodeIO } from "@gltf-transform/core";
135: import { ALL_EXTENSIONS } from "@gltf-transform/extensions";
136: import { MeshoptDecoder } from "meshoptimizer";
137: await MeshoptDecoder.ready;
138: const doc = await new NodeIO().registerExtensions(ALL_EXTENSIONS).registerDependencies({ "meshopt.decoder": MeshoptDecoder }).read(src);
139: await new NodeIO().write(out, doc); // a FRESH NodeIO: one that registered meshopt but has no encoder throws encodeGltfBuffer
140: ```
141: 
142: "Some extensions were not registered for I/O" on write is expected, and the texture still writes.
143: 
144: Simplifying (how the 7k fantasy character was made): `MeshoptSimplifier.simplifyWithAttributes(indices, positions, 3,
145: uvs, 2, [highUvWeight, highUvWeight], null, targetFaces * 3, 1, [])`. Strides are in floats, the target index count must be a
146: multiple of 3, `target_error` up to 1 so the count is actually reached, and the UV weight is high so the texture does not swim.
147: Then `compactMesh`, and write a plain GLB with the original JPEG material.
148: 
149: ### 4.4 Cleanup (every new body goes through this)
150: 
151: From `.impeccable/tools`:
152: 
153: ```
154: python tex-pad.py ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
155: node mesh-clean.mjs ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb --texture ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
156: python mesh-audit.py ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb [yMin]
157: ```
158: 
159: - `tex-pad.py` fills the black gaps between UV islands with the nearest island colour, so seams and mipmaps don't go dark.
160: - `mesh-clean.mjs` drops degenerate triangles, fills small holes, and collapses only tiny folded slivers. Larger folds,
161:   like the shorts hem, are intentional; collapsing them made non-manifold edges. It also recomputes smooth normals shared
162:   across UV seams, and **removes Blender's duplicate unused armature**. A second skin with the same bone names steals the
163:   animation binding, and the body then stays in bind pose. UVs, skin weights and texture are left alone.
164: - Aim for 0 open edges, 0 non-manifold edges and 0 seam normal breaks in the audit.
165: 
166: ### 4.5 Putting a body in the game
167: 
168: All in `useNikoModel` (`world.js`):
169: - Swap `import nikoBody from "./assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb";`. The body is scaled to `PREVIOUS_HEIGHT` 2.17 and yawed
170:   `-Math.PI / 2` (Tripo faces +X; the game walks +Z), with the origin planted at the soles.
171: - Animation is **not** in the GLB. `retargetMixamo` plays `assets/niko/Idle.fbx` and `assets/Running (1).fbx` on any body
172:   with Mixamo bone names. `mixamorig` is stripped on the **target only**; hips keep only their vertical bob.
173: - Lock-on strafes come from `assets/niko/lockon.json` (Pixel Pass Unity `.anim` curves via `lockon-clips.mjs`). Unity
174:   arm curves need the y/z sign flip in `curvesClip` or the wrists cross.
175: - Eyes are painted decals from `assets/niko-eyes.png`, fitted with `EYE_FIT` (`debug.eyes`, `face-fit.mjs`). Hair is
176:   `hair-short.glb` seated on the Head bone (`HAIR_FIT`, `debug.hair`).
177: - An embedded textured body grows the bundle by roughly its file size. Keep bodies around 1.5 MB.
178: 
179: ### 4.6 Verify
180: 
181: - `niko-walk.mjs`, `niko-angles.mjs`, `face-fit.mjs`, `niko-light.mjs` (all in `.impeccable/tools`, screenshots in `.impeccable/review/`).
182: - Prove animation numerically: a bone quaternion changes while a key is held, and the skinned mesh's skeleton bone is the
183:   same object as `bot.bones.<name>`. Screenshot descriptions have invented T-poses before.
184: - `python mesh-audit.py` on the shipped file.
185: 
186: ## 5. Tool index (`.impeccable/tools`)

188: | Tool | Use |

190: | `xiphos-sword.mjs` | Procedural GLB template (run from the repo root) |

192: | `model-view.mjs <url> <prefix>` | Front, side, iso and top shots of any GLB served on :8765 |
193: | `glb-shots.mjs`, `pose-shot.mjs` | Character GLB shots (clips, hands, face) |
194: | `glb-dump.mjs` | Dump a GLB's nodes, materials and textures |
195: | `tex-pad.py`, `mesh-clean.mjs`, `mesh-audit.py` | Body cleanup and audit |
196: | `sword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | In-game pickup and grip shots |
197: | `longsword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | Longsword pickup and left-hand grip check |
198: | `export-kit.mjs` | Exports island pieces to `assets/kit/` for the three.js editor |

10: ## The site
11: - Static GitHub Pages portfolio, vanilla JS. Two views: `classic` (scrolling page) and `world` (3D play mode, default). `?view=classic|world`, remembered in localStorage `fy-view`.

The Pixelage-demo `windField` (-1..1 sway, ×3.2 lean, leaf shear, 46° grass) was tried and REJECTED as ugly/over-bent: keep bends small. Trunk sway weight stays 0. No grass on the beach.

Stairs = stacked slabs + cheek blocks (no sloped curbs). Shadow grain fix: world.js patches PCF `phi` to a constant. Atlas has 3 tiles (bush sprig 0, needles 1, `TWIG_TILE` 2 = tiny tree leaves; user wanted tree leaves small). Bush card .26, s .95–1.35 (knee–hip); tree card .3 on the twig tile; pine card .6. world-check walk waits 120 s.
32: - Effects (ref bruno-simon.com): post always renders to a half-float target; dual-filter bloom (`post` bloom, `?bloom=0`, `debug.post({bloom,threshold,knee,strength})`; user found bloom bled colour: now threshold 1.22 / knee .12 / strength .2 in sRGB units (≈ linear 1.6, only glow() light sources), the intro impact flash sprite was removed (impactLight 35). `THREE.ShaderChunk.colorspace_fragment` is patched to always sRGB-encode (max(rgb,0) first, NaN guard), also into the post target, and the composite does no conversion: linear-space MSAA/blending had made grass and shade paler whenever bloom was on, so bloom on/off now look the same apart from the glow (check: `glow-parts.mjs`, `launch-shots.mjs`); adaptQuality drops DPR to 1, then bloom, then .75). Light sources are HDR: `glow(color, power)`, island `glowing` ×2.4, fire ×2.2. Lamp light: `lampLights` uniform (24 spheres, lanterns + campfire, flicker in `update`) added in `atmos` and `lamped()` (world.js toon/painted/lining, so Niko too). Wind lines = `world-wind.js` (screen-width ribbons, draw-in/loop/wipe, spawn on a random screen point; DoubleSide or they get culled). Tree sway follows the same gust bands (lean capped at 1.05× the baked weight); a fast shake still reads as "someone hitting the tree", so the motion is a traveling wave, not a vibration. Tools: `perf-compare.mjs <urlA> <urlB>` (alternating medians; serve an old build from a `git worktree` with its OWN serve.mjs on another port), `perf-ab.mjs` (A/B toggles, `SOFT=1` SwiftShader for steady ranking), `gpu-profile.mjs`, `cpu-profile.mjs`, `perf-desk.mjs`, `adapt-watch.mjs`, `look-check.mjs` (overcast/fair/night/zoomout shots). +# 3D models: how to regenerate, recreate, or import them
+
+Guide for AI agents working on this repo. Read it before you replace Niko, add a prop from a reference link, or redo a model.
+Project rules still apply (`.cursor/rules/core-memory.mdc`): edit `world.js`, then always run `node .impeccable/tools/build-world.mjs`; CRLF in js/html; never commit unless asked.
+
+## 1. Pick the route first
+
+| What you were given | Route |
+| --- | --- |
+| A link to someone else's model (Sketchfab, ArtStation, a store page) | **B**: recreate it as an original procedural model (route **A**). Download it only if its licence allows it (see section 3). |
+| A Tripo Studio link to a model the user generated | **C**: fetch the user's GLB, decode it, clean it, wire it in. |
+| A GLB the user dropped into `assets/` | **C**, starting from "Cleanup" (section 4.4). |
+| "Make a sword / prop / rock like X" with no file | **A**: write a generator script. |
+
+Never guess. If the user's wording could mean "copy that file" or "make one like it", recreate it (route A) and say so.
+
+## 2. Route A: procedural GLB generator (how the xiphos sword was made)
+
+Reference implementations: `.impeccable/tools/xiphos-sword.mjs` writes `assets/models/xiphos-sword.glb`,
+and `.impeccable/tools/longsword.mjs` writes `assets/models/longsword.glb` (run either from the repo root).
+
+The Sketchfab Longsword by shor.riot (2,524 triangles / 1,531 vertices) is not downloadable, its public API does
+not list a licence, and its page is marked NoAI. The project prop is a generic original weathered-steel longsword
+with a fuller, iron crossguard, wrapped grip, and faceted pommel; it does not include the source mesh, textures, or
+distinctive ornament.
+
+### 2.1 Collect the brief from the reference page
+
+From the reference page, write down the facts that define the look: triangle count, vertex count, texture size,
+materials, and the author's own description. Example, for the Sketchfab xiphos the user linked:
+- 718 triangles / 424 vertices, 256×256 hand-painted diffuse textures, PS2/GameCube "stylized realism".
+- Leaf-shaped bronze blade with patina, heavily worn iron hilt.
+
+Turn that into a shape spec: silhouette (profile stations), cross-section, parts, and palette. Do not trace or download
+their mesh.
+
+### 2.2 Build it in a script, not by hand
+
+The pattern in `xiphos-sword.mjs`:
+- `@gltf-transform/core` `Document` + `NodeIO` writes the GLB; geometry comes from the vendored three
+  (`../../vendor/three/three.module.min.js`): `LatheGeometry` for round parts (grip, pommel), `ExtrudeGeometry` for flat
+  outlines (guard), and hand-built ring lofts for blades (a profile table `[t, halfWidth, halfThickness]` × a cross-section ring).
+- Low-poly look = **faceted**: `geometry.toNonIndexed()` then `computeVertexNormals()`, so every triangle is flat.
+- "Hand-painted" textures = SVG drawn in code and rasterised by `sharp` (gradients, blurred blotches for patina/rust,
+  pits, scratches). Use a **seeded** random so every build is identical. Keep textures small (64–256 px).
+- UVs: blades get u across the width and v along the length (v = 0 at the base; glTF image row 0 is v = 0).
+  Tiling parts use a side projection (`boxUv`) so the texel density matches across pieces.
+- Units and pivot: +Y up along the object's main axis, origin where it is held or stands. The xiphos origin is near
+  the pommel, the guard face at y ≈ 0.2, the tip at y ≈ 0.92, and the grip centre at y = 0.1 (`SWORD_GRIP_Y` in `world.js`).
+- Log the triangle count at the end and keep it near the reference (xiphos: 556 vs the reference's 718).
+
+### 2.3 Preview before wiring
+
+Server: `node .impeccable/tools/serve.mjs 8765` (repo root, background). Then, from `.impeccable/tools`:
+
+```
+node model-view.mjs /assets/models/<file>.glb <prefix>   # writes ../review/<prefix>-{front,side,iso,top}.png
+```
+
+Read the PNGs. The image tool caches by path, so use a new prefix every time.
+
+### 2.4 Wire it into the world
+
+See the sword pickup blocks in `world.js`:
+- `import xiphosGlb from "./assets/models/<file>.glb";`. esbuild's binary loader embeds it in `world.bundle.js`, so `file://` still works.
+- Parse with `new GLTFLoader().parseAsync(buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset + buf.byteLength), "")`.
+- Swap materials to the island look: `node.material = softMapped(node.material.map)`, with `castShadow` and `receiveShadow` on.
+- Size it against Niko: he is about 2.2 world units tall (2.5 units ≈ 1.5 m). The 
<truncated 4650 of 14544 bytes from the middle of the output>
to a file. Do not use PowerShell `curl` (it is Invoke-WebRequest),
+   and do not pass the URL through a shell (the `~` in signatures gets mangled). Signed URLs expire, so download right away.
+   Do not commit or paste the signed URL into docs.
+4. If a quad/retopo mesh is shown in the viewer but never appears in the resources, do not block on it. Simplify locally (4.3).
+
+### 4.3 Decode, and simplify if needed
+
+Run scripts from `.impeccable/tools` (that is where `@gltf-transform/*`, `meshoptimizer`, `sharp` and `puppeteer-core` are installed).
+
+```js
+import { NodeIO } from "@gltf-transform/core";
+import { ALL_EXTENSIONS } from "@gltf-transform/extensions";
+import { MeshoptDecoder } from "meshoptimizer";
+await MeshoptDecoder.ready;
+const doc = await new NodeIO().registerExtensions(ALL_EXTENSIONS).registerDependencies({ "meshopt.decoder": MeshoptDecoder }).read(src);
+await new NodeIO().write(out, doc); // a FRESH NodeIO: one that registered meshopt but has no encoder throws encodeGltfBuffer
+```
+
+"Some extensions were not registered for I/O" on write is expected, and the texture still writes.
+
+Simplifying (how the 7k fantasy character was made): `MeshoptSimplifier.simplifyWithAttributes(indices, positions, 3,
+uvs, 2, [highUvWeight, highUvWeight], null, targetFaces * 3, 1, [])`. Strides are in floats, the target index count must be a
+multiple of 3, `target_error` up to 1 so the count is actually reached, and the UV weight is high so the texture does not swim.
+Then `compactMesh`, and write a plain GLB with the original JPEG material.
+
+### 4.4 Cleanup (every new body goes through this)
+
+From `.impeccable/tools`:
+
+```
+python tex-pad.py ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
+node mesh-clean.mjs ../../assets/niko/<v>.glb ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb --texture ../review/<v>-padded.jpg
+python mesh-audit.py ../../assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb [yMin]
+```
+
+- `tex-pad.py` fills the black gaps between UV islands with the nearest island colour, so seams and mipmaps don't go dark.
+- `mesh-clean.mjs` drops degenerate triangles, fills small holes, and collapses only tiny folded slivers. Larger folds,
+  like the shorts hem, are intentional; collapsing them made non-manifold edges. It also recomputes smooth normals shared
+  across UV seams, and **removes Blender's duplicate unused armature**. A second skin with the same bone names steals the
+  animation binding, and the body then stays in bind pose. UVs, skin weights and texture are left alone.
+- Aim for 0 open edges, 0 non-manifold edges and 0 seam normal breaks in the audit.
+
+### 4.5 Putting a body in the game
+
+All in `useNikoModel` (`world.js`):
+- Swap `import nikoBody from "./assets/niko/<v>-clean.glb";`. The body is scaled to `PREVIOUS_HEIGHT` 2.17 and yawed
+  `-Math.PI / 2` (Tripo faces +X; the game walks +Z), with the origin planted at the soles.
+- Animation is **not** in the GLB. `retargetMixamo` plays `assets/niko/Idle.fbx` and `assets/Running (1).fbx` on any body
+  with Mixamo bone names. `mixamorig` is stripped on the **target only**; hips keep only their vertical bob.
+- Lock-on strafes come from `assets/niko/lockon.json` (Pixel Pass Unity `.anim` curves via `lockon-clips.mjs`). Unity
+  arm curves need the y/z sign flip in `curvesClip` or the wrists cross.
+- Eyes are painted decals from `assets/niko-eyes.png`, fitted with `EYE_FIT` (`debug.eyes`, `face-fit.mjs`). Hair is
+  `hair-short.glb` seated on the Head bone (`HAIR_FIT`, `debug.hair`).
+- An embedded textured body grows the bundle by roughly its file size. Keep bodies around 1.5 MB.
+
+### 4.6 Verify
+
+- `niko-walk.mjs`, `niko-angles.mjs`, `face-fit.mjs`, `niko-light.mjs` (all in `.impeccable/tools`, screenshots in `.impeccable/review/`).
+- Prove animation numerically: a bone quaternion changes while a key is held, and the skinned mesh's skeleton bone is the
+  same object as `bot.bones.<name>`. Screenshot descriptions have invented T-poses before.
+- `python mesh-audit.py` on the shipped file.
+
+## 5. Tool index (`.impeccable/tools`)
+
+| Tool | Use |
+| --- | --- |
+| `xiphos-sword.mjs` | Procedural GLB template (run from the repo root) |
+| `longsword.mjs` | Procedural longsword GLB generator (run from the repo root) |
+| `model-view.mjs <url> <prefix>` | Front, side, iso and top shots of any GLB served on :8765 |
+| `glb-shots.mjs`, `pose-shot.mjs` | Character GLB shots (clips, hands, face) |
+| `glb-dump.mjs` | Dump a GLB's nodes, materials and textures |
+| `tex-pad.py`, `mesh-clean.mjs`, `mesh-audit.py` | Body cleanup and audit |
+| `sword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | In-game pickup and grip shots |
+| `longsword-check.mjs [base] [prefix]` | Longsword pickup and left-hand grip check |
+| `export-kit.mjs` | Exports island pieces to `assets/kit/` for the three.js editor |
+
+When you finish, update `.cursor/rules/core-memory.mdc`. Patch the sentence that changed rather than appending history.

1: ---
2: description: Core memory for Francis Yambao's portfolio. Project state, decisions, build/test workflow. Read first, update at the end of any session that changes something.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Core memory: RigelFrix.github.io
7: 
8: Update this file whenever a task finishes: move items between Done and Open, keep it under ~80 lines, and never copy private details from `.personalinfo/` here.
9: 
10: ## The site
11: - Static GitHub Pages portfolio, vanilla JS. Two views: `classic` (scrolling page) and `world` (3D play mode, default). `?view=classic|world`, remembered in localStorage `fy-view`.
12: - World = Three.js r186 island (concept: `Main Island Concept Board.png`, `Main Island Game Design Overview.png`; feel ref coastalworld.merci-michel.com); Niko walks to stops that open sections/projects. Stops in `world-data.js` (kinds: monolith, hut, skills, milestones, mailbox, lectern; `u`/`v` screen-space position, `faceTo: [u,v]` so stops face their surroundings, never all the camera; `lean`, `scale`).
13: - Brand: cobalt #2430E6, ink #0E0C2B, red #F23A2E, yellow #FFC93C, cream #FFF6E0; one 8° slant everywhere; Big Shoulders Display + Rubik. `html.world` overrides the UI vars with a sea/sky palette (cobalt #2f86d6, ink #102b44...); island palette = `ISLE` in world-island.js.
14: 
15: ## Build and test
16: - Edit `world.js`, then ALWAYS rebuild: `node .impeccable/tools/build-world.mjs` (esbuild to `world.bundle.js`, stamps `?v=hash` in `index.html`). Repo is private, so `.impeccable/`, `.cursor/`, `.agents/`, docs and sampleModels are tracked; only `.impeccable/review/`, `node_modules/`, `.vercel`, `.env*` are gitignored; `.vercelignore` keeps all dev files off the site. New machine: clone, then `npm install` in `.impeccable/tools`.
17: - Server: `node .impeccable/tools/serve.mjs [port]` from repo root (8765, no-cache; Python isn't installed; start in background; user often stops it).
18: - Puppeteer + Edge swiftshader scripts in `.impeccable/tools/`: `intro-check.mjs [base] [outDir must exist] [desktop|mobile|closeup]`, `world-check.mjs [base] [outDir]` (uses `walkTo`, plates are off-screen on the big island), `world-reduced.mjs`, `file-check.mjs`, `island-shots.mjs [base] [prefix] [zoom] "name:u:v,..."`, `walk-trace.mjs <stopId> [u] [v]`, `walk-grid.mjs u0 v0 u1 v1` (ASCII walkable strip), `gl-errors.mjs`. Screens go to `.impeccable/review/`. Debug: `PortfolioWorld.debug.placeUV/zoom/finishIntro/walkable/position/route/bakeShadows`.
19: - 3D models (new prop, recreating a model from a link, swapping Niko's Tripo body): read `.impeccable/docs/3d-models.md` first.
20: - Gotcha: never return a GSAP object from `page.evaluate` (wrap in `void`), it hangs the protocol.
21: - Line endings: CRLF in js/html, LF in `styles.css`.
22: 
23: ## Done
24: - 3D world as default view; `file://` works (bundled IIFE, textures skipped from disk); mobile tap highlight off; tab-switch camera hardening.
25: - Intro (world.js `playIntro`, ~7s, 1.6x on repeat visits via sessionStorage `fy-intro`, any key/tap speeds it up): CSS star twinkles with a load ring, crouches and launches up the 8° lean, cover fades onto a night island, `--dawn` lifts the sky and lights, 3D star falls from just above the screen, impact (flash, shockwaves, debris, shake), robot pops out with a spin-jump and hero pose, then the HUD, name plates and help card arrive. Header stays hidden (`html.world-intro .hud`) until landing unless focused.
26: - Island: `world-map.js` (pure layout, previewed by `.impeccable/tools/map-preview.html`): u = screen right, v = toward camera, `toXZ/toUV`; terraced regions (beach .5, low 3, mid 5.6, top 8.2), stairs, decks (dock, pier, bridge, shrine dais), river, paths, `spots` (landing by the dock, camp, games plaza, shrine...). `world-island.js` `buildIsland`: terrain mesh + rock-column cliffs + props baked into vertex-coloured meshes, water/stream/waterfall shaders, wind grass that parts around Niko, `nav` walk grid + A* (stairs skip the cliff-foot test and allow 0.65 steps), `occlude` (dither scenery in front of Niko), `atmos` (cloud shadows drifting + cool haze near sea level; apply to every lit static material). Zones: shrine + lectern (Resume) at the back, plateau camp (tent About + Skills facing a campfire clearing), ruins stairs + Career stones, cliffside plaza with the 6 game monoliths in a back arc facing its centre, beach/dock start (Contact mailbox on the pier).
27: - Look (user wanted Genshin/BotW feel, not flat): sun from screen upper-left `(-25,30,11)` so shadows fall toward the viewer (a sun behind the camera hid every shadow), warm sun / cool hemi / cool fill, toon ramp `[74,92,186,236,255]`, baked occlusion (`gradeY` on columns/trees, cliff-foot AO + sunlit lips + meadow patches in `groundColour`), CSS grade on `.world-vignette::before/::after` (soft-light sun bloom, faint shafts, cool bottom haze, × `--dawn`). Camera: old look restored, offset (40, 58, 40) so the view looks straight at Niko at ~45.7° down (he sits in the centre). Pitch is live: `debug.angle(degrees)` or `?angle=` (clamped 10–80), and the camera stays on that sphere. Right-drag orbits yaw (0.12°/px, damp 14). Mouse shifts the frame (35% of half-width, 55% of half-height, damp 15); cursor tracking stays active across the visible game under overlays. Follow damp 6–18 with speed. Default yaw is the old diagonal. Middle-click or G locks the training dummy on the spawn court: Niko turns toward it at 720°/s (written on the yaw, a quaternion copy folds past ±90°) and the four run lock-on clips play in that facing (forward, back, left, right). A diagonal blends the two neighbouring run clips, except back-left and back-right, which ease onto `runB` with the hips yawed onto that diagonal and the chest yawed back toward the target. The file's left and right strafes face the other way, so a left move plays the clip labeled right. Lock idle is `assets/niko/Idle.fbx`. Standing still pitches the chest and head up toward the camera (world pitch around his right; the old local rotateX pointed the Mixamo bones the wrong way). The walk quaternion set stays at weight 0. Lock hip curves are scaled ×100 onto the centimeter Mixamo skeleton so the bob stays a bob. A lock-on key press plays the run clip, starting at the frame closest to the current arms. The facing turns on a circle, and a fast left-right swap jumps the aim and crossfades the two run clips instead of dipping through idle. Unity arm curves (shoulders, arms, hands) are stored as (x, -y, -z, w) relative to the FBX, so those two signs are flipped before retarget or each wrist crosses to the other side. Letting go blends the arms back on the short arc. The camera yaw eases behind him (damp 10) and the frame sits halfway between them. Once the yaw is within 18°, either of them leaving the padded screen (or 18 units apart) drops the lock after 0.2 s. Mouse look while locked is clamped so it cannot push them off screen. Intro: Rigel lands on the beach (`landing`) and Niko spawns there; shrine star + beam appear after.
28: - Sharp look (user: colours looked washed/blurry): `makeRamp()` = 3 crisp toon bands shared by island + world.js props (Niko keeps his own ramp), rim 0.06, sun 3.35 / hemi 0.85, shadow radius 1.5, smaller CSS bloom. `groundColour` uses hard `cut()` thresholds (Pixel_Pass-style albedo patches: `grassSun`/`grassShade`/`grassDeep` from separate noises, crisp paths/tide line/camp, 2-step cliff AO) and is baked into a 400² ground texture (`groundTexture`, terrain uv = world xz) plus `grassMask`; `groundAt(x,z)` samples both. Greens are saturated toward Pixel_Pass albedo #71A200.
29: - Look decision (users preferred the GitHub colours): keep the 3-band `makeRamp` [100,176,255], dark ungraded shadows, hard `cut()` patches, 2-step cliff AO, Niko on his own ramp + lavender rim. Rejected: a 2-tone cel ramp + shade/sun colour grade (too flat, shadows too light). Post edge/outline pass in world.js `post` is opt-in (`?fx=1`, `?pixel=3`), off by default. Soft shapes kept: `G.box`/slab = RoundedBox, rocks/blobs = smooth `boulder`, cliff columns smooth, logs/barrels round; world.js `box()` always rounds.
30: - Space + wind: `MAP.K = 1.32` spreads authored uv (`MAP.lay(u,v)`; stops/placeUV use it; widths unscaled), GRID ±44, ground TEX 640. Wind = `WIND_GLSL` `windGust` gust bands rolling along `WIND_DIR` + small base lean, crown roll wave, gentle `aLeaf` (size, phase) flutter; all on `windTime` = climate's integrated wind phase (~1.2/s fair), so strength changes never jump. The Pixelage-demo `windField` (-1..1 sway, ×3.2 lean, leaf shear, 46° grass) was tried and REJECTED as ugly/over-bent: keep bends small. Trunk sway weight stays 0. No grass on the beach.
31: - Assets (after `sampleModels/stylized_bush.glb` + `stylized_low-poly_stone.glb`): rocks = `chisel()` (icosphere pulled onto random planes with `softMin` = flat faces, soft bevels), `G.stones` clusters for big scatter/sea rocks, cliffs = `basalt()` columns. `sized(geo, build)` pieces are rebuilt at real size in `makeBake.add` so bevels never stretch (box, slab, columns). Stairs = stacked slabs + cheek blocks (no sloped curbs). Shadow grain fix: world.js patches PCF `phi` to a constant. Foliage (bush, round tree, pine share it; Niko-scaled): dark `coreBall` core + `leafBall` shell of alpha-tested cards from `foliageTexture()` atlas (tile 0 = small rounded leaf cluster, tile 1 = needle spray), ellipsoid normals, `swayPair` shared sway box, `plant()` puts core in `bake` and cards in `leafBake` (`leafMaterial` + `leafDepth` for shadows). Atlas has 3 tiles (bush sprig 0, needles 1, `TWIG_TILE` 2 = tiny tree leaves; user wanted tree leaves small). Bush card .26, s .95–1.35 (knee–hip); tree card .3 on the twig tile; pine card .6. world-check walk waits 120 s.
32: - Effects (ref bruno-simon.com): post always renders to a half-float target; dual-filter bloom (`post` bloom, `?bloom=0`, `debug.post({bloom,threshold,knee,strength})`; user found bloom bled colour: now threshold 1.22 / knee .12 / strength .2 in sRGB units (≈ linear 1.6, only glow() light sources), the intro impact flash sprite was removed (impactLight 35). `THREE.ShaderChunk.colorspace_fragment` is patched to always sRGB-encode (max(rgb,0) first, NaN guard), also into the post target, and the composite does no conversion: linear-space MSAA/blending had made grass and shade paler whenever bloom was on, so bloom on/off now look the same apart from the glow (check: `glow-parts.mjs`, `launch-shots.mjs`); adaptQuality drops DPR to 1, then bloom, then .75). Light sources are HDR: `glow(color, power)`, island `glowing` ×2.4, fire ×2.2. Lamp light: `lampLights` uniform (24 spheres, lanterns + campfire, flicker in `update`) added in `atmos` and `lamped()` (world.js toon/painted/lining, so Niko too). Wind lines = `world-wind.js` (screen-width ribbons, draw-in/loop/wipe, spawn on a random screen point; DoubleSide or they get culled). Tree sway follows the same gust bands (lean capped at 1.05× the baked weight); a fast shake still reads as "someone hitting the tree", so the motion is a traveling wave, not a vibration. Grass trampling: `trail` RT ping-pong (rg lean×amount, b amount; soft 0.58 stamp, decay ~0.7/s ≈3 s). Standing = flatten only (no radial crater; tips scatter toward camera); walking = lean along the step. Grass shader: mild screen roll, height squash, world tipPush, wind ×(1−0.92·press). Check: `trail-shot.mjs`. Loop dt is clamped ≥ 0 (settle made it negative). Tools: `trail-shot.mjs`, `wind-peek.mjs`, island-shots env `JS`.
33: - Controls: floating touch stick in world.js (`stick`, `.world-stick`; a touch that drags > 12 px becomes the stick where the drag began, base stays fixed, knob clamps at the 46 px rim, light push = slower walk via `state.pace`, which also scales the run clip); a short tap/click still walks. Zoom: wheel + two-finger pinch (`touches`, `pinch`) feed `zoomBy` → `zoomGoal`, eased in `easeZoom` (play 0.7–1.7; intro tweens camera.zoom directly). `debug.zoom(z)` is the only way past that: down to 0.25 to see more of Niko, and the wheel keeps 0.25–8 until `debug.zoom(null)`. `zoom-check.mjs` tests wheel, pinch, fixed stick.
34: - Perf (measured with `perf-check.mjs [base] [dpr] [cpuThrottle]`, headful real GPU, env SHORT/Q): the offscreen HDR target + MSAA resolve cost 2–4x the scene itself; grass/leaves/props each only ~5 ms at 3x. So: `lite` (coarse, or `?lite=1`; `?lite=0` opts out) renders straight to the screen (no post), DPR cap 2 everywhere (`MAX_RATIO`), island `halos` (additive sprites on lanterns/fire + shrine inlay disc) show whenever bloom is off; offscreen MSAA only below 1.5x DPR (`?msaa=1/0`); depth texture only with `?fx=1`. adaptQuality (real frame time, hitches capped at 250 ms) ladder: MSAA off → bloom off → DPR −0.25 down to 1, then only while still > 34 ms down to `MIN_RATIO` 0.6 (climbs back toward 1 under 14 ms); > 60 ms takes all steps at once. 5: ---
6: 
7: # PixelPass vertex VFX recipe
8: 
9: Every PixelPass lit pass (ForwardLit, ShadowCaster, DepthOnly, DepthNormals) runs object-space position through `PixelPassApplyVertexEffects`. Outlines read depth/normals, so a VFX that skips those passes desyncs the silhouette.
10: 
11: ## Add a VFX
12: 
13: ```hlsl
14: // PixelPassApplyVertexEffects
15: positionOS = PixelPassApplySmear(positionOS);
16: positionOS = PixelPassApplyYourEffect(positionOS);
17: ```
18: 
19: - Put math in its own header. Strength `0` must be a no-op.
20: - Append uniforms to `PIXELPASS_VERTEX_EFFECT_PROPERTIES` (must stay inside `UnityPerMaterial`, same order in both `*Input.hlsl` files).
21: - Copy matching `[HideInInspector]` Properties into **both** `CelCharacterLit.shader` and `StylizedToonLit.shader` or `HasProperty` / MPB fails.
22: - Drive per renderer with `MaterialPropertyBlock`. Create it in `Awake`, never a MonoBehaviour field initializer (`CreateImpl` exception).
23: - Include children when the skinned mesh is not on the moving root. CPU mesh cloning cannot smear `SkinnedMeshRenderer`.
24: 
25: ## Never
26: 
27: ```hlsl
28: // BAD — UsePass cannot run the hook; shadows/outlines stay unsmeared
29: UsePass "Universal Render Pipeline/Lit/ShadowCaster"
30: ```
31: 
32: ```csharp
33: // BAD
34: readonly MaterialPropertyBlock _block = new MaterialPropertyBlock();
35: ```
36: 
37: - Do not duplicate `UnityPerMaterial` per pass; include `CelCharacterLitInput.hlsl` / `StylizedToonLitInput.hlsl`.
38: - Do not put VFX constants in a second CBUFFER; MPB overrides only reach `UnityPerMaterial`.
39: - Do not `[ExecuteAlways]` deform `sharedMesh` (bakes runtime meshes into the scene).
40: - `UsePass .../Meta` is intentional (lightmap bake, no VFX).
41: 
42: ## Cluster lights
43: 
44: URP 17 `_CLUSTER_LIGHT_LOOP` forces `_ADDITIONAL_LIGHTS` and `LIGHT_LOOP_BEGIN` reads `inputData`. Call `PixelPassInitForwardInputData` at the top of every lit `Frag` before any light loop. Dropping it pinks both character shaders.
45: 
46: ## Weak spots — do not “clean up” unless asked
47: 
48: - Cel and Toon **Frag** light loops are duplicated on purpose (per-shader look).
49: - `StylizedToonLit` keeps a large URP-compat Properties block so imported Lit materials remap.
50: - Pixel size lives on `PixelPerfectGrid`; the volume only multiplies it by whole steps.
51: - Smear tracks the mover pivot by default, not bone motion.
52: - Shared pass files replace URP Lit geometry passes; keep shadow bias via `ApplyShadowBias` + `ApplyShadowClamping`.

# SmearFrame
"Smear frame" material effect for Unreal Engine 4.12

![Smear Frame effect](http://i.giphy.com/l46CcnrPYQsJ0ejw4.gif "UE4 Smear Frame effect")

## What is this?
This is an Unreal Engine 4 project containing a simple implementation of a "smear frame" effect, as recently popularized by the game Overwatch.

## How do I use this?
This effect consists of two parts: a blueprint component you add to an actor you want to be affected by the smear frame effect, and a material function that you add to its material.

## Limitations
As a quick and dirty proof of concept, this effect uses the actor's velocity to determine smear strength. As such, it does not work with animated skeletal meshes in the way you'd expect. Suggestions or pull requests are very welcome though! :)

![Smear Frame effect](http://broad-strokes.com/media/smear.gif "UE4 Smear Frame effect")

## Credits
Created by Jan Kaluza of [Broad Strokes](http://www.broad-strokes.com) ([@JKashaar on Twitter](https://twitter.com/JKashaar)).

Inspired by Blizzard's Overwatch, as well as Twitter user [@MercurialForge](https://twitter.com/MercurialForge/status/747871518575648768)

Add a stylistic **idle animation**, a stylistic **running animation**, and a first mechanic: **heavy right-hand punch** with a whole-arm smear effect referencing `https://github.com/RigelFrix/Pixel_Pass` (`C:\Users\Rigel\Documents\PersonalGitHub\Pixel_Pass\Assets\PixelPass\ShaderLibrary\PixelPassSmear.hlsl` & `PixelPassSmearEffect.cs`).

     - **Read `https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/free-smear-frame-effect-download-project-from-github/67822`** (Jan Kaluza's `LuggLD/SmearFrame` UE4 project) and **improve the arm smear effect** so it is no longer rigid/blocky, stretches smoothly from the arm mesh itself, and includes a **motion-blur effect on the moving part of the mesh**.

## 2. Progress
- **Completed:**
  - Read and analyzed `https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/free-smear-frame-effect-download-project-from-github/67822` (`67822.json`) and its GitHub repository `https://github.com/LuggLD/SmearFrame` (`Content/SmearFrame/SmearFrame.uasset`, `SmearFrameComponent.uasset`, and GIFs `ue-smear-1-peak.png`, `ue-smear-2-peak.png`).
  - Updated `.impeccable/tools/werewolf-boss.mjs` to add `subdivideStations()` and `smooth: true` support to `loft()` and `spikeGeo()`, upgrading the boss's arms/forearms/hands (`UpperArm`, `ShoulderMark`, `ShoulderFurTop`, `ShoulderFurLow`, `ForeArmBulk`, `ElbowSpike`, `ForearmMark`, `WristWrap`, `Palm`, `Finger`, `HandClaw`, `Thumb`, `ThumbClaw`) to **smooth welded vertex normals** (`computeVertexNormals()` on indexed geometry) with `14` radial segments and `3x` axial station subdivision.
  - Regenerated `assets/models/werewolf-boss.glb` (8,922 triangles) via `node .impeccable/tools/werewolf-boss.mjs`.
  - Created three modular handler files in the repo root (matching `world-island.js`, `world-climate.js`, `world-wind.js`, `world-rain.js`, `world-rays.js`):
    1. `world-smear.js` (`createSmearHandler`): Reusable Smear Frame + Sub-Frame Motion Blur handler combining:
       - UE4 `LuggLD/SmearFrame` World Position Offset (`dot(VertexNormalWS, -smearDir) + uSmearNormalBias` × 3-octave 3D Fast Gradient Noise `smearFbm` in `WPT_ExcludeAllShaderOffsets` cross-motion space),
       - `Pixel_Pass` (`PixelPassSmear.hlsl` & `PixelPassSmearEffect.cs`) 4-frame lag queue, speed factor ramp, per-axis travel clamp, and asymmetric `followSharpness` / `releaseSharpness` damping,
       - Fragment-stage directional motion-blur lighting softener + stylistic brush-streak grading + feathered streak-tip alpha fade (`gl_FragColor.a *= smearAlpha`),
       - 4 translucent **sub-frame motion-blur ghost shells** (`bindLimbGhostBlur`) of `RightArm` + `RightForeArm` posed across sub-frame timestamps along the swing arc so the moving part of the arm mesh has genuine geometric & visual motion blur.
    2. `world-boss-anim.js` (`BOSS_PUNCH_DURATION`, `computeBossPose`, `applyBossPoseDirect`): Dedicated Boss Animation Pose & Joint Articulation handler for `"idle"`, `"run"`, and `"punch"`.
    3. `world-boss.js` (`createWerewolfBoss`): Dedicated Werewolf Boss entity, loader, state machine, and combat mechanic handler.
- **In Progress (Next Immediate Action):**
  - Replace the inline boss & smear block in `world.js` (lines 15, 2057–2876, 5072, 5902–5931) with a clean import of `createWerewolfBoss` from `./world-boss.js`.

## 3. Key Findings
- **Why the Previous Arm Smear Looked Rigid and Blocky (and How `LuggLD/SmearFrame` Solves It):**
  1. **Mesh Normals & Vertex Density (`SmearFrame.uasset`):** `LuggLD/SmearFrame` uses `dot(VertexNormalWS, -SmearDir) + SmearNormalAngleBias` multiplied by 3D Fast Gradient Noise (`WPT_ExcludeAllShaderOffsets`) and explicitly notes: *"Mesh vertex density needs to be relatively high for this to look good"*. Previously, `werewolf-boss.mjs` called `geo.toNonIndexed()` (`faceted`) on 3-station, 8-sided arm cylinders, causing each flat triangle to have a discontinuous face normal and stretch into blocky, rigid slabs. Switching the arm meshes to **indexed, welded smooth normals (`smooth: true`)** with `14` radial sides and `3x` subdivided rings (`werewolf-boss.mjs`) gives a continuous `VertexNormalWS` field that pulls out fine, organic brush fibers directly from the arm mesh.
  2. **Motion Blur on the Moving Part of the Mesh:** In `ue-smear-1-peak.png` and `ue-smear-2-peak.png`, the moving object is blurred across sub-frames and its stretched streak tips feather out softly while retaining the object's shaded colors. `world-smear.js` achieves this via:

     - Feathering alpha at the stretched streak tips (`tipFade`),
